subject: Unexpected spike on November invoice - HybridAI migration tokens
messages:
From: Alex Nguyen <alex@hybridai.io>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Unexpected spike on November invoice - INV-2026-11-331

Hi Kimberly,

We just received invoice INV-2026-11-331 and noticed a ~1.1M token spike in line items attributed to an internal process called 'hybrid-migrator' that we don't recognize as production traffic. This pushed our month-over-month spend up ~72% and put the invoice on hold while we sort VAT and payment.

Can you please provide:
- Raw per-request logs for 2026-11-01 00:00 to 2026-11-01 12:00 UTC (request ids and model variant)
- Clarification on how tokens were attributed to our billing entity (we have both HybridAI Ltd (UK) and HybridAI GmbH (DE) in the account)
- An expedited credit for any inadvertent staging/migration traffic billed to production

We need this information for our finance team to release payment; also flagging VAT concerns — if the tokens belong to our EU entity (GmbH) we may need reverse-charge handling.

Attaching a screenshot of the invoice line (attachment: usage_snapshot_20261101.csv).

Thanks,
Alex Nguyen
CFO, HybridAI

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex@hybridai.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected spike on November invoice - INV-2026-11-331

Hi Alex — thanks for the heads up and sorry for the confusion. We can absolutely dig into this fast.

Quick asks from our side to speed the audit:
- Confirmation that the time window above (2026-11-01 00:00–12:00 UTC) is the entire suspicious window you see; if there are other times, please add them.
- Which legal entity should we apply any credit to (HybridAI Ltd or HybridAI GmbH)? VAT handling depends on that.

What we'll do immediately:
- Pull raw request-level logs (unaggregated) and a token-attribution trace for the window you specified.
- Run a tag/label reconciliation to see if any migration jobs used prod keys or a mis-tagged service account.
- Provisionally reserve a credit while we investigate; this would be applied as a one-off credit on the next invoice pending root-cause.

I'm attaching our quick request form for approvals (attachment: request_form.pdf) — please sign/confirm and return so finance can expedite. Ben, can you take the lead on the log pull and attribution?

Kimberly Park
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T14:25:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: initial findings on HybridAI spike

Kim / Steph — quick summary of what I pulled from telemetry (preliminary):
- Time window: 2026-11-01 02:07:12 UTC — 2026-11-01 04:18:34 UTC shows the highest token density.
- ~1,067,540 tokens total during window; of those, ~850,432 tokens originated from requests authenticated with a key tied to HybridAI but labeled in our telemetry as 'staging/hybrid-migrator'.
- There is a pattern where a CI migration orchestration (internal service named hybrid-migrator) ran a bulk data transform and appears to have picked up a production API key due to a config flip during a rollout. The requests used model redwood-giant-v1 with typical completion lengths (avg 120 tokens).

Action items I recommend:
1) Reclassify the 850,432 tokens from "billable/production" to a non-billable staging migration bucket where possible, or issue credit if reclassification cannot be retroactive.
2) Provide HybridAI a per-request CSV (request_id, timestamp, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, api_key_tag) — I pushed the export to gs://redwood-telemetry/hybridai/20261101-logs for the audit.
3) Add an internal policy to block CI service accounts from hitting production endpoints without an explicit allow list.

I'm also attaching the usage snapshot CSV for the window (usage_snapshot_20261101.csv).

Ben Carter
Billing Operations — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex@hybridai.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T08:09:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected spike on November invoice - INV-2026-11-331 (proposal)

Hi Alex — following up with what we found and a proposed remediation.

Summary:
- Root cause: CI migration job (hybrid-migrator) incorrectly used a production API key during a rollout; telemetry shows ~850,432 tokens attributable to that job between 2026-11-01 02:07–04:18 UTC.
- Status: We uploaded per-request export to gs://redwood-telemetry/hybridai/20261101-logs and attached a CSV snapshot to this thread (usage_snapshot_20261101.csv).

Proposed remediation (to resolve the invoice hold):
1) Retroactive credit of 850,432 tokens. Based on your subscribed rate tier, this equates to a provisional credit of $3,426.56 applied to your next invoice (INV-2026-12-001).
2) VAT handling: please confirm which legal entity the billed tokens should be associated with (HybridAI Ltd — UK or HybridAI GmbH — DE). If it should be the EU GmbH we will reissue the credit and adjust VAT (reverse-charge) on the corrected invoice.
3) Operational fix: we will implement the CI blocklist and perform a weekly audit of service-account usage for 90 days; we'll share the summary of the first audit within 7 business days.

Next steps for you:
- Reply to confirm the legal entity for credit/VAT handling and confirm whether the provisional credit amount is acceptable.
- If you want us to proceed with a customer-facing credit now (so finance can release payment), reply "APPROVE CREDIT" and we'll queue the adjustment immediately.

We regret the disruption and will follow up with the audit evidence package for your records.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123
